captive_summary: PowerMagazine's own reporting documents PAWA PNG as an integrated floating storage/regasification-and-power system: 'FSRP power barges, which include power generators and regasification equipment, and where power generation from gas turbines and waste energy takes place,' feeding twelve 'power island' locations across PNG at an aggregate 283 MW (unit sizes 8.6-21.9 MW). hardware_summary: Multiple aero-derivative gas turbine generators (one held in standby) providing primary electrical power (base load 44,000 kW / 44.267 MW, sized up to 59,760 kW with 20% growth + 15% contingency allowance) PLUS separate aero-derivative gas turbines shaft-driving the refrigerant/liquefaction compressors (mechanical drive, no electricity generated); diesel-engine generators are provided separately for essential/black-start power only (non-gas, out of scope).
fuel_basis: Project's EIS states both the compressor-drive turbines and the power-generation turbines are 'fuelled by the high-pressure fuel gas system' (feed gas / process gas / boil-off gas); aero-derivative technology explicitly chosen over frame-turbine technology for lower emissions.
captive_summary: PNG LNG's Environmental Impact Statement (Chapter 4, a primary regulatory filing) documents a fully self-contained power system: gas turbine generators (one in standby) meet an estimated 44,000 kW base electrical load (Table 4.1: LNG trains 20,060 kW + storage 10,847 kW + utilities 5,782 kW + offsites 3,753 kW + camps 3,825 kW = 44,267 kW total, growing to 59,760 kW with margins), all fuelled by the plant's own high-pressure fuel gas system. Separately, aero-derivative gas turbines mechanically drive the refrigerant compressors (shaft power, not generation) — the base case selected specifically over heavier frame-turbine technology for lower emissions. Diesel-engine generators exist only for black-start/essential backup and are excluded (non-gas).
mechanical_drive_note: Aero-derivative gas turbines drive the refrigerant-circuit compressors (frame vs. aero-derivative technology compared in the EIS; aero-derivative selected as base case) — shaft power only, no generator; aggregate MW/shaft-hp not disclosed in this chapter.
confirmed_how: https://www.pnglng.com/media/PNG-LNG-Media/Files/Environment/EIS/eis_chapter04.pdf (Chapter 4, Environmental Impact Statement, a primary regulatory document): Section 4.2.3.4 'Power Generation and Distribution Systems' — 'A number of gas turbine generators (one of which will be in standby mode) will produce electrical power to meet an estimated base load of 44,000 kW (Table 4.1)... The turbine generators will be fuelled by the high-pressure fuel gas system.' Table 4.1 itemizes the 44,267 kW base load and 59,760 kW total with growth/contingency. Section 4.2.2 (Turbines for the Refrigeration System Compressors): 'The refrigerant circuits will require gas turbine generators to drive the compressors... The base case for the refrigeration system compressor turbines is the aero-derivative technology.' Essential/black-start power is separately 'Diesel-engine-driven generators.'
